findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.comment:
3-501.14: Inspector found Tuna salad, made in house, at 51F when temperature was taken with a probe thermometer. The tuna salad was constructed and put to cool at 8am today. The probe temperature was taken at 2:15 pm. The tuna has been in the temperature danger zone for 6 hours and 15 minutes. The tuna salad will be discarded. The tuna salad is double panned in plastic with a tight fitting lid. Inspector suggests putting tuna in the walk in freezer to cool after it is constructed. Stir tuna salad in order to help remove heat from the salad. 5 lbs of tuna salad was discarded in the garbage. Take care to use effective cooling techniques such as covering lightly, single panning or placing in an environment that is cold enough to remove the heat from the product. The hang thermometer is reading 43F. The unit has been open on top for the lunch service period and appears to be going through a defrost cycle. These factors add up when cooling. Place tuna in a cooling unit when cooling not a make table. 

(A) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within in 2 hours from 135F to 70F. Within 6 hours, FOOD shall cool from 135F to 41F or less. (B) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within 4 hours or less if prepared from ingredients at ambient temperature. (C) TCS FOOD received above 45F in compliance with LAWS shall be cooled within 4 hours. (D) Raw EGGS shall be received and immediately placed in EQUIPMENT with air temperature of 45F or less.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.  

Observed the manager on duty to only be a food handler, not a certified food protection manager. It appears there is only one currently for the facility (main manager). The facility will need at least 1 more CFPM, if not 2 more in order to have a certified food protection manager available during all operational hours. Manager on duty was unaware of paperwork needed by SCDPH and Inspector helped him find the necessary paperwork in the filing cabinet. The public health paperwork and licenses should be readily available at any point in time. The file has not been updated with copies of food handler’s licenses and CFPM licenses, employee health reporting agreements, Norovirus illness clean-up policy, etc. When prompted about test strips, manager on duty has never seen them at the facility (therefore, test strips are not being routinely used to check sanitizer concentrations). When prompted about sani bucket/spray bottle process, manager on duty stated they use soap and water on food-contact surfaces, sometime dipping rags within the, “sanitize”, basin of the 3 compartment sink and cleaning. The facility needs a set rule on how to properly wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces. All staff should be made aware. Test strips should be used to check concentrations. Facility is utilizing quaternary ammonium - 200 to 400 ppm, change sanitizer every 4-6 hours to keep concentration appropriate. Inspector will follow-up on 10/3/22.

Ensure to wash hands with soap, hot water, and dry hands with a paper towel. Ensure a barrier to used to turn off faucet handles such as a paper towel in order not to re-contaminate hands. findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. 

Observed no working sanitization bucket upon inspection. Discussed with PIC. Upon questioning, it was noted that facility is not regularly sanitizing with a sani bucket or spray bottle. Soap and water are used to sanitize food-contact surfaces or rags dipped in the quaternary ammonium at the 3 compartment sink. In-use rags should be in their own sani bucket with quaternary ammonium. Spray bottles of sanitizer may be used if the spray bottle is labeled, “sanitizer”, and paper towels are utilized to wipe surfaces. Ensure to used test strips to check concentration and change buckets/spray bottles every 4-6 hours to maintain appropriate concentration. Quaternary ammonium: 200-400 ppm. COS. Provided sanitization log due to lack of awareness in importance of sanitizer use.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
The following items were measured with temperatures greater than 41F (located in the South facing 3 door make table cooler): sliced salami 47F, roast beef 52F, ham 45F, turkey 47F, cut lettuce 50F, sliced tomatoes 53F. Staff indicated food items were placed into cooler less than 2 hours to inspection. Lid was observed open during busy times during inspection. Ambient temperature of cooler measured 39F.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 - A) Employee entered service area after going to the back hallway and began to put on gloves without washing hands. Employee was advised that hands need to be washed prior to putting on gloves and was asked if he just came from the restroom. Employee stated he had. Employee washed his hands prior to putting on gloves for sandwich prep.

B) Employee previously assembling sandwiches was observed wearing only one glove and disposing of a paper towel. Employee was then observed preparing to put on a new glove. When asked what she did with the paper towel that was just discarded, the employee stated she wiped her nose. The employee was advised hands needed to be washed prior to putting on a new pair of gloves. Employee washed hands and put on a new pair of gloves to finish sandwich prep.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated, before putting on gloves, between glove changes, after using the restroom, upon entering service area and before beginning food prep, and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles.
Handwashing and glove use educational materials were provided.

Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4). Maintain Steramine solution at 200-400ppm as directed on label, and use test strips to ensure the sanitizing concentration is correct.

CORRECTED = Mop was hung up.
750-1390 Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similar equipment shall be maintained and stored in a way that does not contaminate food.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.comment: There is no stem thermometer on site to check the temperatures of food in the facility. 750-230 A calibratable metal-stemmed thermometer accurate to ±2F° shall be provided for checking temperatures on food. Provide thermometer.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment: Personal soda and water (open) are stored in the walk in cooler above food for service to the public. 750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination. Remove soda and water or provide proper place for employee food storage such as a bus tub below foods for public consumption.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: The soda nozzles in the facility are soiled in the aeration holes of the nozzles. 750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use. Use a brush to properly clean nozzles so that soil does not accumulate.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.comment: Bottle of sanitizer being used on the slicer is not labeled. 750-1300 Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances. Sanitizer bottle was labeled.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Top layers of cheese, roast beef, turkey, ham, & salami in top holding area of sandwich prep cooler had surface temperatures at 59F-64F. Layers of product were stacked above the top rim of the pans and lid was open. Surface temperatures in lower layers were at 43F/below, and an internal temperature of 40F was observed when a stem thermometer was used to check the temperature of meat. Guacamole, mayo, and Grey Poupon were at 50F and 46F respectively. Guacamole was double panned and not down in direct contact with cold are in holding compartment. Top layers of meats and cheese were removed/discarded. Mayo, guacamole, and Grey Poupon were switched out with fresh product.
Potentially hazardous foods (PHF) shall be maintained at 41F/below unless time control is being used. Place smaller quantities of products in pans and close lid during slow periods to help maintain colder temperatures for PHF. Time control may be used if the time is tracked and products are used or discarded w/in 4hrs. Management noted a permanent change would be established for either storage of foods (less product/lid closed) or time control policy would be established. A time control policy sheet was provided.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text: 750.510 - Employee was observed shutting of manual faucet with bare hands prior to drying his hands. Employees must properly wash hands whenever hands may have been contaminated, before putting on gloves, between glove changes, and between tasks/as needed. Proper handwashing technique was discussed. Educational handouts were provided on proper handwashing (Section 750.510 of IL Food Code), when to wash hands, and proper use of single use gloves.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.citation_text: 750.820 - Employee was observed briefly dunking equipment in sanitizer solution during ware washing process at 3 part sink. Proper sanitizing was discussed with employee and management. Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4). Proper manual ware washing handout was provided.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Sanitizer solution in bucket tested at 0ppm chlorine. Bucket of solution was emptied. Discussed use of buckets versus spray bottles for sanitizer solutions. If spray bottles will be used for storage of sanitizer solutions make sure bottles are properly labeled and maintained at 100ppm. Use fresh paper towels and discard after use. If buckets are maintained, then change solutions every 2 to 4 hours or more often when solutions and wiping cloths become heavily soiled, and store wiping cloths in solution between uses.
Concentrations for sanitizing solutions used for general surfaces and clean in place equipment must be at 100ppm.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled: A) crevice on surface on sprayer at 3 part sink and B) ice shoot at soda machine. Clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris. **In-use utensils and equipment (i.e. knives, cutting boards, slicer, etc.) must be properly cleaned and sanitized at least every 4hrs.**

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.citation_text: 750.1170 - Door sweep was observed to be cracked and light was visible at the bottom of the front door. A door sweep was replaced during the inspection. Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects. Maintain outer openings tight fitting/vermin proof; change door sweeps and weather stripping as needed.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text: 750.1220 - Floor drain below 3 part sink was soiled with grimy buildup. Clean the floor drain as needed and maintain clean.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.citation_text:
750.1300 - Spray bottles of blue liquid were observed without proper labels. Bottles were labeled as to the contents (window cleaner). Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Maintain proper labels on containers of toxic substances.
Never rely on color or smell for identification of a chemical.
